source_topology_binding.source_only_bridge_analysis: The finite-sum bridge must allow arbitrary (not separately assumed measurable) limits Q_j. Finite measure and measurability of the approximants suffice. The residual sum is signed and converges in measure; the original sequence is not claimed to converge pathwise.

source_evidence.anchor: Original Samplinglib supplement: Coordinate quadratic variation controls the vector Taylor residual. Exact assumptions and formula below.
source_evidence.statement: In a finite-dimensional Euclidean state space, it suffices that the square-increment sum of each coordinate converge in measure to its own real-valued Qⱼ. The vector Taylor residual sum then converges in measure to zero.
assumptions: I is a finite coordinate set, E=ℝᴵ with its Euclidean norm, Ω carries a finite measure μ, and K⊆E is compact.
f:E→ℝ is C² at every point of K. The K-valued process X has measurable evaluations at every nonnegative time and almost-sure continuous paths on [0,T], where T>0.
For each j∈I the dyadic square-increment sum of coordinate j converges in measure to Qⱼ:Ω→ℝ.
source_evidence.boundary: The coordinate variation limits are inputs here. The result includes any finite coordinate set and claims convergence in measure, not pathwise convergence of the original sequence.
